ai.summary: Uris Design is a Next.js portfolio workspace with a live, voice enabled AI assistant that can talk about projects, skills, and implementation details, and can also navigate the site to the relevant section while the conversation unfolds.
ai.tagline: A frontend portfolio built as a conversational screening and navigation surface.

header.title: Conversational AI Portfolio Screening
header.subtitle: A Next.js portfolio and frontend engineering showcase. Visitors can ask about projects, skills, and implementation details through a live, voice enabled AI conversation, and the assistant can open the relevant project, skills, or contact section in response.

items.title: AI-first portfolio workspace
items.description: The site is structured as a workspace instead of a brochure: a central AI conversation surface, draggable side panels, project browsing, and settings that support live exploration and guided navigation.

items.title: Realtime voice conversation
items.description: WebRTC powers full-duplex voice interaction with a dedicated `oai-events` data channel for model events, transcript updates, and connection-aware UI behavior.

items.title: Static project delivery with dynamic loading
items.description: Project routes are generated statically from a central map, while each detail page is loaded on demand so the app stays scalable without shipping every case study up front.

items.title: Store-driven interaction model
items.description: Separate Zustand stores manage connection lifecycle, talking state, response history, and active streaming output so realtime behavior stays predictable as the interface grows.

items.title: Built on Slice
items.description: The product reuses my own UI and browser runtime library for theme, layout, media, notifications, and WebRTC primitives, turning the site into a real application of the system rather than a standalone mock.

blocks.text: Traditional portfolios are mostly static brochures. They show work, but they do not let someone properly screen a candidate, ask follow-up questions, or quickly move from one project to another based on interest.

Imagine a recruiter, founder, or hiring manager saying "I want to understand your experience with design systems, AI, or realtime product work" and getting a direct, guided, conversational path through your work and background, with the site opening the relevant project or skills section as part of that exchange.
Imagine that as a candidate you can save simply point an AI at your work (json, site, github, npm) and have the AI automatically support and present your work to anyone interested.

This is also a small showcase piece for Next.js fluency. The app uses the App Router, server-rendered layout setup, static generation for project detail routes, route handlers for session orchestration, and a server-side project content store that pre-renders each project page from structured JSON.

That matters here because the app has two very different responsibilities: render content quickly like a polished portfolio, and then progressively layer in realtime voice and client state where interactivity is needed.

items.label: Realtime conversation
items.text: WebRTC handles live audio transport with a single `oai-events` data channel for model events. The microphone stream is attached to the connection, and assistant updates arrive as typed data messages that are parsed into state updates and UI callbacks.

items.label: State orchestration
items.text: `viStore` manages connection lifecycle, talking state, and event callbacks, while `responsesStore` owns the response history and active streaming response shown in the UI.

items.label: Next.js delivery model
items.text: Project routes are generated statically from a central server registry, while page content is transformed from structured project JSON into UI-ready data for pre-rendered project detail pages.

items.label: Shared backend boundary
items.text: Session creation is proxied through a dedicated API layer shared across products. That keeps the Next.js app focused on product experience while reusing the same backend integration model elsewhere.

items.label: Route generation and delivery
items.text: Project detail pages are generated from known project slugs, with `generateStaticParams()` producing static routes and server-side transformers shaping the same project JSON into page, tile, and AI-specific views.

items.label: Assistant data awareness
items.text: The assistant is seeded with project summaries on session start and can request structured project and skills data through explicit tools, giving it grounded content to talk about instead of relying on vague prompt-only context.

items.label: Client and server separation
items.text: Theme resolution and layout bootstrapping happen through the App Router layout, while interactive surfaces such as the AI panel, settings, and project workspace hydrate on the client where stateful behavior is needed.

items.label: Realtime event handling
items.text: Assistant events like `session.created`, `response.output_audio_transcript.delta`, and `response.output_audio_transcript.done` are routed through a dedicated event handler that updates store state without coupling transport logic to UI components.

items.label: Navigation actions
items.text: The assistant can trigger browser-side view changes for projects, skills, contact, and selected UI settings, so conversation is tied directly to movement through the site instead of being isolated from the interface.

items.label: Voice and device control
items.text: Microphone access, input volume, mute state, and device selection are managed through Slice primitives and synchronized back into the WebRTC connection so the live assistant stays in step with the selected input device.

items.label: Workspace UI composition
items.text: The app is structured as a multi-panel workspace with draggable side surfaces, a central AI thread, settings, toast/tip systems, and project detail rendering instead of a single linear landing page.

items.label: Shared integration model
items.text: The Next.js route handler acts as an app-facing boundary for session requests, while the reusable backend API handles the external realtime session creation used by this project and others.

items.label: A conversational portfolio model
items.text: The site is built around asking natural questions about skills, projects, and background instead of forcing users through a click-heavy path.

items.label: Grounded assistant behavior
items.text: The assistant can talk about projects and skills from structured server data rather than acting as a generic voice shell with no awareness of the portfolio content.

items.label: Realtime interface engineering
items.text: Live voice input, streaming assistant output, and event-driven UI updates coordinated through WebRTC and typed store logic.

items.label: Conversational navigation
items.text: The model can open the relevant section of the site on request, turning voice conversation into an actual browsing control layer instead of leaving navigation entirely to the user.

items.label: Practical Next.js architecture
items.text: App Router composition, static route generation, route handlers, and server/client boundaries used for real product reasons.

items.label: Frontend systems thinking
items.text: The implementation ties routing, realtime state, media/device handling, and interface composition into one coherent product instead of treating them as isolated features.

items.label: Design system reuse
items.text: The product is built on Slice, my own UI and browser runtime library, which lets the app reuse the same primitives for theme, layout, media, and WebRTC handling.

items.label: Extensible tool surface
items.text: The current tool layer already supports project detail lookup, skills awareness, view navigation, and selected settings updates, with room to extend the model without rewriting the interface model.

blocks.text: Making conversation useful — the hard part is not just connecting to a model. It is shaping the portfolio so conversation becomes a real navigation and discovery layer, not a novelty. The implemented tool surface is what starts turning this from "chat on a site" into "screen this person naturally."

Balancing fast content with live systems — the app needs to feel like a fast, well-structured website first, while still supporting live audio, connection state, and streaming assistant responses once a user chooses to engage.

Keeping boundaries clean — the site, the shared API layer, and the Slice library each have different responsibilities. Keeping those seams intentional is part of the engineering quality, not just the implementation detail.

End-to-end product and implementation: concept, interaction model, Next.js app architecture, realtime AI integration, state design, UI system usage through Slice, and the shared API boundary used to support this app and other products.
